paper.title: On Upper-Confidence Bound Policies for Non-Stationary Bandit Problems

settings.name_in_paper: Abruptly changing environment (non-stationary MAB with breakpoints)
unmapped: Rewards bounded in [0,B] with B known to the algorithm (used in padding function); recorded as bounded_01 up to scaling
Regret measured against the arm with highest mean at each time t; Upsilon_T (= S_T) breakpoints before T
settings.definition_quote: we consider abruptly changing environments: the distributions of rewards remain constant during periods and change at unknown time instants called breakpoints. In the following, we denote by $\Upsilon_T$ the number of abrupt changes in the reward distributions that occur before time $T$.

settings.name_in_paper: Abruptly changing environment, tuned parameters (known T and Upsilon_T)
unmapped: Rewards bounded in [0,B] with B known; recorded as bounded_01 up to scaling
Regret against the best arm at each time
settings.definition_quote: If horizon $T$ and the growth rate of the number of breakpoints $\Upsilon_T$ are known in advance, the discount factor $\gamma$ can be chosen so as to minimize the RHS

settings.name_in_paper: Piecewise constant rewards with two breakpoints (lower bound)
unmapped: Lower bound relates regret under a mixture of modified (two-breakpoint) environments to regret under the stationary environment
settings.definition_quote: we consider a particular non-stationary bandit problem where the distributions of rewards on each arm are piecewise constant and have two breakpoints.

symbols.C_gamma: (gamma-1)/(log(1-gamma) log gamma) * log((1-gamma) xi log N_K(gamma))
symbols.Delta_mu_T(i): minimum over t<=T with i not optimal of mu_t(*)-mu_t(i)

source.label: th:boundbadplayed
source.quote: Let $\xi>1/2$ and $\gamma\in(0,1)$. For any arm $i\in\{1,\dots,K\}$, \E_{\gamma}[\tilde N_T(i)] \leq \operatorname{B}(\gamma) T (1-\gamma) \log \frac{1}{1-\gamma} + \operatorname{C}(\gamma)\frac{\Upsilon_T}{1-\gamma}\log \frac{1}{1-\gamma}

results.notes: Bounds expected number of times arm i is played while not optimal, not regret directly. Upsilon_T mapped to S_T. Algorithm does not use T, but bound is for horizon T.

Bound on expected number of suboptimal plays of arm i; paper also states regret O(T^{(1+beta)/2} log T) when Upsilon_T=O(T^beta), and O(sqrt(Upsilon T) log T) for bounded Upsilon. Hidden constants depend on Delta_mu_T(i), B, xi.

bound.regime: number of breakpoints bounded by Upsilon independently of T

source.label: rk:gammaofRn
source.quote: In particular, if $\beta=0$, the number of breakpoints $\Upsilon_T$ is upper-bounded by $\Upsilon$ independently of $T$, taking $\gamma=1-(4B)^{-1}\sqrt{\Upsilon/T}$, the regret is bounded by $O\left( \sqrt{\Upsilon T}\log T \right)$.

results.notes: Upsilon mapped to S_T. Regret obtained by summing pull-count bounds over arms; constants hide K and gaps.

symbols.Delta_mu_T(i): minimum over t<=T with i not optimal of mu_t(*)-mu_t(i)

source.label: th:boundbadplayedwindow
source.quote: Let $\xi>1/2$. For any integer $\tau$ and any arm $i\in\{1,\dots,K\}$, \E_{\tau}[\tilde N_T(i)]\leq \operatorname{C}(\tau)\frac{T\log\tau}{\tau} + \tau \Upsilon_T +\log^2(\tau)

results.notes: Bound on expected number of plays of arm i while it is not optimal.

source.quote: Taking $\tau=2B\sqrt{T\log(T)/\Upsilon_T}$ yields $\E_{\tau}[\tilde N_T(i)]= O( \sqrt{\Upsilon_T T\log T} )$.

results.notes: Pull-count bound; paper also states regret O(T^{(1+beta)/2} sqrt(log T)) when Upsilon_T=O(T^beta).

bound.regime: number of breakpoints bounded by Upsilon independently of T

source.quote: In particular, if $\beta=0$, the number of breakpoints $\Upsilon_T$ is upper-bounded by $\Upsilon$ independently of $T$, then with $\tau=2B\sqrt{T\log(T)/\Upsilon }$ the upper-bound is $O\left( \sqrt{\Upsilon T\log T} \right)$.

results.notes: Paper says 'the upper-bound' (ambiguous between pull count and regret); interpreted as regret as in the conclusion.

symbols.R_stat: expected regret E_pi[R_T] of the policy in the stationary environment
symbols.delta_nu: nu - mu(1), gap of the modified arm K distribution Q

conditions: left side is regret under a uniform mixture of environments where arm K's distribution switches to Q on one epoch (two breakpoints)

source.label: th:binf
source.quote: For any policy $\pi$ and any horizon $T$ such that $64/(9\alpha)\leq \Es[\Np[T][]{K}]\leq T/(4\alpha)$, \E_\pi^*[R_T] \geq C(\mu)\frac{T}{\E_\pi[R_T]}, where $C(\mu)=\frac{32\delta(\mu(1)-\mu(K))}{27\alpha}$.

results.notes: Stated for deterministic policies; Remark 15 says it extends to randomized ones. Implies that policies with logarithmic stationary regret suffer T/log T regret with breakpoints (Remark 16).

conditions: bound on the max of the stationary regret and the regret under the mixture of two-breakpoint environments

source.quote: For any policy $\pi$ and any positive horizon $T$, $$\max\{\E_\pi(R_T), \E_\pi^*(R_T)\} \geq \sqrt{C(\mu)T}\eqsp.$$

results.notes: Distributions are fixed (do not shrink with T).

cited_results.setting_description: Non-stationary / adversarial K-armed bandit, regret against strategies with Upsilon_T switches, Upsilon_T known
